title: Advanced pronouns and placement
objectives: I can place object pronouns correctly in formal Portuguese using enclisis, proclisis and mesoclisis.
I can recognize combined pronouns such as mo, to and lho in formal and literary texts and replace them in everyday speech.
I can identify and use the different roles of se: reflexive, reciprocal, passive, impersonal and inherent.
I can place pronouns with ir plus infinitive and with compound tenses, in both formal and colloquial Brazilian usage.

vocabulary.note: Always used with se; it does not exist without the pronoun.

example.pt: Arrependo-me de não ter estudado mais.
example.en: I regret not having studied more.

vocabulary.note: More formal than reclamar. Followed by de.

example.pt: Os moradores queixaram-se do barulho.
example.en: The residents complained about the noise.

example.pt: Dirija-se ao balcão de atendimento.
example.en: Go to the service counter.

example.pt: Comprometo-me a entregar o relatório na segunda.
example.en: I commit to delivering the report on Monday.

vocabulary.note: Lembrar without se means to remind someone or, in casual speech, to remember. The pronominal form is the careful one.

example.pt: Lembro-me bem daquele dia.
example.en: I remember that day well.

example.pt: Ninguém se atreveu a contradizê-lo.
example.en: Nobody dared to contradict him.

example.pt: Dei-me conta do erro tarde demais.
example.en: I realized the mistake too late.

vocabulary.en: to meet (each other); to be located
vocabulary.note: Reciprocal when the subject is plural, and a formal substitute for estar when the subject is a thing.

example.pt: Encontramo-nos às oito na praça.
example.en: We meet at eight in the square.

example.pt: Os colegas cumprimentaram-se com um aperto de mão.
example.en: The colleagues greeted each other with a handshake.

vocabulary.note: Mutuamente or uns aos outros removes any doubt between the reciprocal and the reflexive reading.

example.pt: Os vizinhos se ajudam mutuamente.
example.en: The neighbors help one another.

example.pt: Eles se entendem sem precisar falar.
example.en: They understand each other without having to speak.

vocabulary.note: Formal way to say that an event happens.

example.pt: A audiência realizar-se-á na sexta-feira.
example.en: The hearing will take place on Friday.

vocabulary.note: The same form is used for women: a requerente.

example.pt: O requerente deverá apresentar os documentos.
example.en: The applicant must present the documents.

example.pt: O signatário declara ter lido o contrato.
example.en: The signatory declares having read the contract.

vocabulary.en: to grant, to approve a request
vocabulary.note: Administrative and legal verb; conjugates like preferir.

example.pt: O pedido foi deferido ontem.
example.en: The request was granted yesterday.

example.pt: A prefeitura indeferiu o requerimento.
example.en: The city hall rejected the application.

example.pt: A entrada é liberada mediante a apresentação do comprovante.
example.en: Entry is allowed upon presentation of the receipt.

vocabulary.note: Very formal; found mostly in legal and official writing.

example.pt: Informo, outrossim, que o prazo foi prorrogado.
example.en: I further inform you that the deadline was extended.

example.pt: A cláusula quinta trata do prazo de pagamento.
example.en: The fifth clause deals with the payment deadline.

example.pt: O prazo para a entrega termina na sexta.
example.en: The deadline for delivery ends on Friday.

example.pt: Vamos notificá-lo por escrito.
example.en: We will notify him in writing.

example.pt: O remetente da carta não se identificou.
example.en: The sender of the letter did not identify himself.

example.pt: O destinatário mudou-se e não deixou endereço.
example.en: The recipient moved and left no address.

vocabulary.en: the filing number, the reference receipt
vocabulary.note: In Brazilian bureaucracy, the number you receive when you file a request.

example.pt: Guarde o número do protocolo para consultar o processo.
example.en: Keep the reference number to check on the case.

dialogues.title: No balcão da prefeitura
dialogues.context: Dona Helena goes to the city hall to ask about an application she filed three weeks ago. The clerk, Seu Antunes, uses formal register.

lines.speaker: Helena
lines.pt: Bom dia. Dirijo-me ao senhor para saber do meu requerimento de alvará.
lines.en: Good morning. I am addressing you to ask about my permit application.

lines.speaker: Antunes
lines.pt: Bom dia, senhora. Qual é o número do protocolo? Encontra-se no comprovante que lhe entregaram.
lines.en: Good morning, ma'am. What is the reference number? It is on the receipt they gave you.

lines.speaker: Helena
lines.pt: Aqui está. Entreguei-o há três semanas e ninguém me deu resposta.
lines.en: Here it is. I handed it in three weeks ago and nobody gave me an answer.

lines.speaker: Antunes
lines.pt: Vou verificar. O processo ainda não foi deferido, mas o resultado ser-lhe-á comunicado por escrito até sexta.
lines.en: I will check. The case has not yet been granted, but the result will be communicated to you in writing by Friday.

lines.speaker: Helena
lines.pt: Se eu me queixar na ouvidoria, isso adianta alguma coisa?
lines.en: If I complain to the ombudsman's office, does that help at all?

lines.speaker: Antunes
lines.pt: Pode queixar-se, mas o prazo legal ainda não terminou. Aconselho-a a aguardar.
lines.en: You may complain, but the legal deadline has not yet ended. I advise you to wait.

lines.speaker: Helena
lines.pt: Entendo. Comprometo-me a voltar na sexta, então.
lines.en: I understand. I will commit to coming back on Friday, then.

lines.speaker: Antunes
lines.pt: Perfeito. Se o pedido for indeferido, informá-la-emos de imediato.
lines.en: Perfect. If the request is rejected, we will inform you immediately.

lines.speaker: Helena
lines.pt: Muito obrigada. Não me esquecerei disso.
lines.en: Thank you very much. I will not forget this.

lines.speaker: Antunes
lines.pt: Disponha, senhora. Tenha um bom dia.
lines.en: You are welcome, ma'am. Have a good day.

dialogues.title: Escrevendo uma carta formal
dialogues.context: Sofia must write a formal letter to her bank. Her friend Bruno, who works in a law office, explains where the pronouns go.

lines.speaker: Sofia
lines.pt: Bruno, me ajuda com essa carta? Tenho que escrever para o banco e não sei onde colocar os pronomes.
lines.en: Bruno, can you help me with this letter? I have to write to the bank and I don't know where to put the pronouns.

lines.speaker: Bruno
lines.pt: Na fala a gente diz me dá uma resposta, mas numa carta se escreve dê-me uma resposta.
lines.en: In speech we say me dá uma resposta, but in a letter you write dê-me uma resposta.

lines.speaker: Sofia
lines.pt: E se a frase tiver uma palavra negativa, tipo não?
lines.en: And if the sentence has a negative word, like não?

lines.speaker: Bruno
lines.pt: Aí o pronome vai antes do verbo: não me informaram, não lhe disse.
lines.en: Then the pronoun goes before the verb: não me informaram, não lhe disse.

lines.speaker: Sofia
lines.pt: E com o futuro? Quero dizer que vou enviar os documentos ao gerente.
lines.en: And with the future? I want to say that I will send the documents to the manager.

lines.speaker: Bruno
lines.pt: Pode escrever enviar-lhe-ei os documentos, só que soa muito solene. Hoje muita gente prefere vou enviar-lhe os documentos.
lines.en: You can write enviar-lhe-ei os documentos, but it sounds very solemn. Today many people prefer vou enviar-lhe os documentos.

lines.speaker: Sofia
lines.pt: Já vi mo e lho em livros antigos. Ninguém fala assim, né?
lines.en: I have seen mo and lho in old books. Nobody talks like that, right?

lines.speaker: Bruno
lines.pt: Na fala, ninguém. A gente diz ele me deu isso. Mo, to e lho só aparecem em textos jurídicos e na literatura.
lines.en: In speech, nobody. We say ele me deu isso. Mo, to and lho only appear in legal texts and in literature.

lines.speaker: Sofia
lines.pt: Então vou escrever: peço-lhe que examine meu pedido e me comunique a decisão.
lines.en: Then I will write: I ask you to examine my request and communicate the decision to me.

lines.speaker: Bruno
lines.pt: Isso! Depois da palavra que, o pronome vem antes do verbo. Sua carta está ótima.
lines.en: Exactly! After que, the pronoun comes before the verb. Your letter is excellent.

dialogues.title: Reunião de condomínio
dialogues.context: Neighbors meet to discuss noise complaints and a planned barbecue. Several uses of se appear naturally.

lines.speaker: Marcos
lines.pt: Boa noite a todos. Vamos começar. Primeiro ponto da pauta: as reclamações sobre o barulho.
lines.en: Good evening everyone. Let's begin. First item on the agenda: the noise complaints.

lines.speaker: Ana
lines.pt: Alguns moradores queixam-se do som alto depois das dez, e ninguém sabe a quem se dirigir.
lines.en: Some residents complain about loud music after ten, and nobody knows whom to approach.

lines.speaker: Tavares
lines.pt: Eu me arrependo de ter comprado neste prédio. Antes, os vizinhos se ajudavam, e hoje ninguém se fala.
lines.en: I regret buying in this building. Before, the neighbors helped each other, and today nobody talks to anyone.

lines.speaker: Marcos
lines.pt: Entendo, seu Tavares. Mas vendem-se cada vez mais apartamentos aqui, e as pessoas novas ainda não se conhecem.
lines.en: I understand, Mr. Tavares. But more and more apartments are being sold here, and the new people don't know each other yet.

lines.speaker: Ana
lines.pt: Por isso proponho um churrasco. Assim os moradores se encontram e se conhecem melhor.
lines.en: That is why I propose a barbecue. That way residents meet and get to know each other better.

lines.speaker: Tavares
lines.pt: Boa ideia. Mas precisa-se de alguém para organizar tudo.
lines.en: Good idea. But someone is needed to organize everything.

lines.speaker: Marcos
lines.pt: Eu me comprometo a cuidar da lista. Vocês podem ajudar-me com as compras?
lines.en: I commit to handling the list. Can you help me with the shopping?

lines.speaker: Ana
lines.pt: Claro, eu o ajudo. Vou lhe mandar os nomes amanhã.
lines.en: Of course, I will help you. I will send you the names tomorrow.

lines.speaker: Tavares
lines.pt: E se alguém reclamar, dirija-se a mim. Não me importo de explicar.
lines.en: And if anyone complains, come to me. I don't mind explaining.

lines.speaker: Marcos
lines.pt: Combinado. A reunião encerra-se às nove. Vemo-nos no sábado!
lines.en: Agreed. The meeting closes at nine. See you on Saturday!

grammar.title: Enclisis, proclisis and mesoclisis
grammar.explanation:
Object pronouns (me, te, o, a, lhe, nos, se) can stand before the verb (proclisis), after it with a hyphen (enclisis) or inside a future or conditional verb (mesoclisis). In Brazilian speech, proclisis is the overwhelming default, even at the start of a sentence: me dá um cigarro, te vejo amanhã, me disse que vinha. Formal writing follows the stricter rule, which is based on European usage.

In formal written Portuguese, enclisis is the normal position in an affirmative main clause with no attractor: disse-me, encontramo-nos, dirijo-me. Certain words attract the pronoun to the front of the verb, and proclisis is then required: negatives (não, nunca, ninguém, nada, jamais), subordinating conjunctions (que, se, quando, embora, porque), relative pronouns, interrogative words (quem, como, onde), and some adverbs such as já, também, sempre and ainda.

Mesoclisis places the pronoun between the stem and the ending of the future or the conditional when nothing attracts it: dar-lhe-ei, dir-me-ia, realizar-se-á. It is now rare even in writing, and when an attractor is present the pronoun simply goes before the verb: não lhe darei. In everyday formal writing, most people avoid mesoclisis by rephrasing with ir plus infinitive or with the present.

examples.pt: Informo-lhe que o pedido foi deferido.
examples.en: I inform you that the request was granted.
They never told me that.
I hope you understand me.
I will send you the reply tomorrow.

examples.pt: Se me permite, gostaria de acrescentar algo.
examples.en: If you allow me, I would like to add something.

examples.pt: Dir-se-ia que ninguém percebeu o erro.
examples.en: One would say that nobody noticed the mistake.

grammar.title: Combined pronouns and their colloquial substitutes
grammar.explanation:
When an indirect object pronoun (me, te, lhe, nos, vos, lhes) meets a direct object pronoun (o, a, os, as), formal and literary Portuguese fuses them: me plus o becomes mo, te plus a becomes ta, lhe plus os becomes lhos. The first-person plural and second-person plural forms keep a hyphen and lose the s or the ending: nos plus o becomes no-lo, vos plus o becomes vo-lo.

These forms belong almost entirely to legal, administrative and literary registers: Entreguei-lho ontem, A notícia, ninguém ma contou. In Brazilian speech they have disappeared. Speakers use other strategies: repeat the pronoun as a full prepositional phrase (entreguei pra ele), use the indirect pronoun alone and drop the object (ele me deu, with the object already understood), or use the stressed pronoun as the direct object (eu vi ele), which is normal in speech but avoided in writing.

Remember also that the direct object pronoun o, a, os, as takes a different shape after certain verb endings: lo, la, los, las after r, s or z (fazê-lo, vendemo-la, fi-lo), and no, na, nos, nas after a nasal sound (dão-no, põe-na). These changes also appear in enclisis in ordinary formal writing.

examples.en: The book? I lent it to him yesterday.

examples.pt: Ela quis a chave, e eu entreguei-lha.
examples.en: She wanted the key, and I handed it to her.

examples.pt: Pediu o contrato, e mandaram-no logo.
examples.en: He asked for the contract, and they sent it right away.
I will do it today.

examples.pt: Ele me deu isso de presente e nunca me pediu nada.
examples.en: He gave me this as a present and never asked me for anything.

grammar.title: The many functions of se
grammar.explanation:
The word se is one of the busiest in Portuguese, and the grammatical role determines the agreement of the verb. It can be reflexive (the subject acts on itself: ela se olhou), reciprocal (plural subjects act on each other: eles se abraçaram), passive (the thing is the subject and the verb agrees with it: vendem-se casas), impersonal (no specific subject; the verb stays singular: precisa-se de ajudantes, vive-se bem aqui, trata-se de um erro), inherent (the verb exists only with se: arrepender-se, queixar-se, atrever-se) and emphatic (optional reinforcement: ele foi-se embora).

To tell the passive from the impersonal, look at the verb. If it is transitive and takes a direct object, the object becomes the subject and the verb agrees in number: aluga-se apartamento, alugam-se apartamentos. If the verb is intransitive or takes a preposition, the verb stays in the third person singular: precisa-se de motoristas, fala-se de política.

In speech, Brazilians often replace se-constructions with a plural verb (vendem casas) or with a gente and você. The passive se still dominates in signs and advertisements, and the inherent verbs keep se in all registers.

examples.en: Apartments are sold in this neighborhood.
A driver with experience is needed.

examples.pt: Os dois irmãos se abraçaram na rodoviária.
examples.en: The two brothers hugged each other at the bus station.

examples.pt: Ela arrependeu-se de ter vendido a casa.
examples.en: She regretted having sold the house.
It is a matter of an administrative error.

grammar.title: Pronouns with ir plus infinitive and compound tenses
grammar.explanation:
With an auxiliary plus main verb, the pronoun has several possible positions. In formal writing it attaches to the infinitive or to the auxiliary: vou dizer-lhe, quero vê-lo, tinha-me dito, tenho-me esforçado. An attractor pulls it before the auxiliary: não lhe vou dizer, não me tinha dito.

The pronoun never attaches to a participle: tinha-o visto, never tinha visto-o. In the gerund the enclitic form is used in writing (estou procurando-o).

In everyday Brazilian Portuguese, the pronoun is placed before the main verb and after the auxiliary, without a hyphen: vou lhe dizer, quero te ver, tinha me dito, tenho me esforçado, estou te procurando. Native speakers consider these forms natural, even if traditional grammars label them as errors. Use the formal position in exams, letters and contracts, and the colloquial one in conversation. For the third-person direct object, speech prefers to drop the object or use ele and ela: quero ver ele, where writing would have quero vê-lo.

rows: Vou lhe dizer. Vou te falar.
Quero te ver. Quero ver ele.

examples.en: I will send you the documents tomorrow.
She had warned me about the delay.

examples.pt: Não lhe quero dizer isso agora.
examples.en: I do not want to tell you that now.

examples.pt: Estou te esperando desde as oito.
examples.en: I have been waiting for you since eight.
I want to see her as soon as possible.

culture.title: A gramática escolar e a fala brasileira
culture.text:
Pronoun placement is one of the clearest differences between written and spoken Brazilian Portuguese, and between Brazilian and European Portuguese. In Portugal, enclisis is the rule in ordinary speech: dá-me, disse-me, vejo-te amanhã. In Brazil, people say me dá, me disse and te vejo amanhã, and a sentence that begins with an enclitic pronoun sounds formal, even solemn.

The tension between school rules and real speech has a long literary history. In the 1920s, the Modernist poet Oswald de Andrade mocked the grammar book in a short poem called Pronominais, contrasting the textbook line Dê-me um cigarro with the everyday Me dá um cigarro. The point was to defend the Brazilian way of speaking as legitimate.

For learners, the practical lesson is to control both. Brazilian official and legal documents, academic texts, newspaper editorials and the questions on national exams such as the ENEM and public service tests keep the formal rules. The expression juridiquês is used humorously for the heavily formal language of lawyers, with its mesoclisis, mo and lho. In conversation, however, insisting on dá-me may sound stiff. Choose the register to fit the context.

paragraphs.pt: Prezado senhor gerente, dirijo-me a Vossa Senhoria para solicitar a revisão de uma cobrança que considero indevida.
paragraphs.en: Dear Manager, I am addressing you to request a review of a charge that I consider improper.

paragraphs.pt: Em março, pedi o cancelamento do meu cartão de crédito. Informaram-me de que o pedido fora registrado, mas a fatura de abril chegou com uma anuidade de duzentos reais.
paragraphs.en: In March I requested the cancellation of my credit card. They informed me that the request had been registered, but the April bill arrived with an annual fee of two hundred reais.

paragraphs.pt: Procurei a agência duas vezes. Em nenhuma delas me deram uma explicação clara; disseram-me apenas que o sistema estava com problemas.
paragraphs.en: I went to the branch twice. On neither occasion did they give me a clear explanation; they only told me that the system was having problems.

paragraphs.pt: Caso a cobrança seja mantida, ver-me-ei obrigada a recorrer à ouvidoria e ao órgão de defesa do consumidor.
paragraphs.en: If the charge is maintained, I will be obliged to appeal to the ombudsman's office and the consumer protection agency.

paragraphs.pt: Comprometo-me a enviar, em anexo, cópias do protocolo e das faturas. Peço-lhe que me comunique a decisão no prazo de dez dias.
paragraphs.en: I commit to sending, attached, copies of the reference receipt and the bills. I ask that you communicate the decision to me within ten days.

paragraphs.pt: Agradeço desde já a atenção e coloco-me à disposição para esclarecimentos. Atenciosamente, Marta Ribeiro.
paragraphs.en: I thank you in advance for your attention and remain at your disposal for clarifications. Sincerely, Marta Ribeiro.

questions.prompt: What is the main purpose of the letter?
choices: To open a new credit card
To request a review of an improper charge
questions.explanation: She asks for the revisão de uma cobrança indevida.

questions.prompt: Why does Marta believe the charge is improper?
choices: The fee was higher than in the contract
She had asked to cancel the card before the fee appeared
questions.explanation: She canceled the card in March but was still charged an annual fee in April.

questions.prompt: What did the bank staff tell her at the branch?
choices: That the system was having problems
That the card was already canceled
That she should write a letter
questions.explanation: They said only that o sistema estava com problemas.

questions.prompt: What will she do if the charge is kept?
choices: Go to the ombudsman and to the consumer protection agency
questions.explanation: Ver-me-ei obrigada a recorrer à ouvidoria e ao órgão de defesa do consumidor.

paragraphs.pt: A gramática escolar ensina que não se deve iniciar uma frase com pronome oblíquo. Assim, o professor corrige quem diz me dá um cigarro e pede que se diga dê-me um cigarro.
paragraphs.en: School grammar teaches that a sentence should not begin with an object pronoun. So the teacher corrects whoever says me dá um cigarro and asks that dê-me um cigarro be said.

paragraphs.pt: Na fala espontânea dos brasileiros, no entanto, o pronome vem quase sempre antes do verbo. Ninguém diz dá-me o sal à mesa; todos dizem me passa o sal, por favor.
paragraphs.en: In the spontaneous speech of Brazilians, however, the pronoun almost always comes before the verb. Nobody says dá-me o sal at the table; everyone says me passa o sal, por favor.

paragraphs.pt: Essa diferença separa o português do Brasil do europeu, em que a ênclise é a regra nas frases afirmativas. Em Portugal, dizer me disse soaria estranho; no Brasil, dizer disse-me soa formal.
paragraphs.en: This difference separates Brazilian from European Portuguese, in which enclisis is the rule in affirmative sentences. In Portugal, saying me disse would sound odd; in Brazil, saying disse-me sounds formal.

paragraphs.pt: Escritores modernistas, como Oswald de Andrade, transformaram o assunto em poesia e defenderam a fala brasileira. Hoje, a norma escrita continua mais conservadora do que a fala.
paragraphs.en: Modernist writers such as Oswald de Andrade turned the subject into poetry and defended Brazilian speech. Today the written standard remains more conservative than speech.

paragraphs.pt: Para o estudante estrangeiro, o caminho mais seguro é dominar as duas formas: usar a próclise na conversa e a ênclise em cartas, contratos e provas de concurso.
paragraphs.en: For the foreign student, the safest path is to master both forms: use proclisis in conversation and enclisis in letters, contracts and civil service exams.

questions.prompt: What does school grammar say about starting a sentence?
choices: It should begin with a verb only
It should not begin with an object pronoun
It should always begin with a pronoun
It should begin with a conjunction
questions.explanation: School grammar says não se deve iniciar uma frase com pronome oblíquo.

questions.prompt: How do Brazilians usually place the pronoun in spontaneous speech?
questions.explanation: The text says o pronome vem quase sempre antes do verbo.

questions.prompt: What does the text recommend to foreign students?
choices: Master both proclisis and enclisis and use each in its context
Use only the formal forms everywhere
questions.explanation: The advice is to use proclisis in conversation and enclisis in formal writing.

exercises.prompt: Which is the correct formal way to say 'Tell me the truth'?
exercises.explanation: In formal writing an affirmative command takes enclisis: diga-me.

exercises.prompt: Which sentence follows the formal rule?
exercises.explanation: The negative word não attracts the pronoun to the front of the verb.

exercises.prompt: Which form is an example of mesoclisis?
exercises.explanation: In mesoclisis the pronoun sits inside the future verb: dar-lhe-ei.

exercises.prompt: What is the function of se in Vendem-se casas?
exercises.explanation: Casas is the subject and the verb agrees with it in the plural: passive se.

exercises.prompt: In Precisa-se de motoristas, why is the verb singular?
choices: Precisar takes a preposition, so se is impersonal and the verb stays singular
It is a mistake in the sentence
exercises.explanation: Precisar de takes a prepositional object, so there is no subject for the verb to agree with.

choices: I handed it to him yesterday.
I handed it to myself yesterday.
I did not hand it over yesterday.
He handed it to me yesterday.
exercises.explanation: Lho is lhe plus o: 'it to him or her'.

exercises.prompt: How would most Brazilians say Tinha-me dito in conversation?
exercises.explanation: Colloquial Brazilian puts the pronoun before the main verb without a hyphen.

exercises.prompt_pt: Informo-___ que o pedido foi deferido.
exercises.hint_en: I inform you (sir or ma'am) that the request was granted.
exercises.explanation: Lhe is the indirect object pronoun for o senhor and a senhora.
The negative word não puts the pronoun before the verb.
After que the pronoun goes before the verb.

exercises.prompt_pt: Eles deram o livro para mim. Eles deram-___ ontem.
exercises.hint_en: They gave it to me yesterday.
I will send you (sir) the documents tomorrow.
exercises.explanation: In mesoclisis the pronoun appears between the infinitive and the ending -ei.

exercises.prompt_pt: Ela arrependeu-___ de ter vendido a casa.
exercises.hint_en: She regretted having sold the house.
exercises.explanation: Arrepender-se is an inherent pronominal verb.

exercises.hint_en: I will send you (sir) the reply tomorrow.
exercises.explanation: With ir plus infinitive, formal writing attaches the pronoun to the infinitive.

exercises.prompt_en: I did not tell him anything.
answers: Eu não disse nada a ele.
Eu não disse nada para ele.
Eu não disse nada pra ele.
A gente se encontra na sexta.
A gente se encontra na sexta-feira.

exercises.prompt_en: I am addressing you, sir, to ask for information.
They did not tell me anything about this.
I commit to delivering the report.

I inform you that the request was lost.

exercises.prompt: Match the combined pronoun with its meaning

pairs.en: te + a (her or it to you)
lhe + o (it to him or her)

exercises.prompt: Match the administrative term with its meaning
